transcript:
--- Meeting Header ---
Date: 2025-05-21 15:00 PDT
Duration: 57 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Ramirez (Redwood AE), Ethan Cole (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (FinServX CISO), Arjun Patel (FinServX Head of Ops), Leah Brooks (FinServX SRE), Tomáš Novák (FinServX Compliance)
Recorded: Zoom auto-record

--- Auto-generated Summary (may be imperfect) ---
Redwood walked through incident response and BCDR expectations; discussed SLA, payloads, RTO/RPO, audit logs, KMS. Action items assigned.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00:05] Sofia: Hey everyone welcome, thanks for carving out time, quick intro — I'm Sofia Ramirez, AE on the account, with Ethan and Priya from our engineering team.
[00:00:12] Maya: Hi all, Maya here — thanks. We're particularly focused today on the incident response runbook and how that ties into your BCDR and SLA commitments.
[00:00:20] Ethan: Great, yeah we'll walk through our standard escalation flows, RTO/RPO tiers, and where customers can expect notification and compensation if anything degrades.
[00:00:30] Arjun: Two quick context points: 1) Our product is latency-sensitive for trading use-cases so availability is critical; 2) Compliance needs to sign-off on any cross-region failovers for EU data.
[00:00:40] Priya: Noted — we'll call out data residency boundaries and optional manual failover gating.
[00:01:05] Tomáš: On SOC2, we need to know the evidence package you can provide — are there audit logs with immutable retention?
[00:01:15] Ethan: Yes, audit logs are collected at the control plane level and we can provide log exports; retention settings are configurable per contract. Note: logs are append-only in our storage and we can provide WORM exports for auditors.
[00:01:30] Maya: And KMS? Who owns keys in a Private deployment?
[00:01:35] Sofia: For Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS — we integrate with cloud KMS or HSMs. For Hosted, we use encrypted-at-rest with our managed keys by default but customer-managed keys (BYOK) is available on Dedicated/Private tiers.
[00:02:10] Leah: If we have BYOK, how does the rekeying flow look during failover? Does the secondary region get access to keys?
[00:02:18] Ethan: We have a documented rekey and replication plan — keys can be replicated under your control depending on your KMS policies. If you block cross-region key export, failover becomes manual until keys are provisioned in the DR region. That affects RTO.
[00:02:45] Arjun: Let's talk numbers — what RTO and RPO should we expect for critical traffic on Dedicated vs Hosted?
[00:02:52] Priya: For Dedicated we target RTO 15 minutes for service-level platform issues with automated failover in the same region, and RPO under 5 minutes for in-memory KV caches that are checkpointed. For cross-region DR we design for RTO 1–3 hours depending on key replication and warm standby config.
[00:03:20] Maya: 1–3 hours is a big window; for regulated trading flows that's borderline. Is hot-warm an option?
[00:03:27] Ethan: Yes, we offer hot-standby in a second region for mission-critical customers — that reduces RTO to 15–30 minutes but increases cost substantially (double the capacity). We can present cost/benefit.
[00:03:45] [00:03:46] Maya: (murmur) okay
[00:04:10] Sofia: On SLA, our standard for Dedicated enterprise customers is 99.95% monthly uptime with financial credits per the contract. We typically map incident severity to notification SLAs: P0 — page within 5 minutes and bridge within 15, exec notification within 60 minutes; P1 — page within 15 and resolution target 4 hours, etc.
[00:04:40] Arjun: How are incidents detected? Relying on our metrics or do you run synthetic checks?
[00:04:48] Priya: Both — platform health is monitored via synthetic probes, internal telemetry, and customer-facing metrics. We also support customer-supplied healthchecks. Alerts route through PagerDuty with escalation policies.
[00:05:10] Leah: For runbooks, can we merge our alerts into your oncall? We don't want noisy double notifications.
[00:05:18] Ethan: Absolutely, we can federate alerts via PagerDuty or webhook. We usually recommend a single source of truth for paging thresholds and then run a dedup policy so incidents aren't duplicated.
[00:05:40] [00:06:05] Maya: About legal and e-discovery — will audit logs be suitable for forensic requests? Chain-of-custody?
[00:06:12] Sofia: We provide exportable logs that include timestamps, actor identities (SSO/SCIM user IDs), and actions. For forensics we can provide signed exports, and for Private deployments these exports can be retained in your storage with your retention policy.
[00:06:40] Tomáš: Do you have tabletop exercise examples or a runbook template?
[00:06:45] Priya: Yes, we have a tabletop kit and IR runbook template — we'll share an editable version. Recommended cadence is quarterly exercises for critical customers.
[00:07:05] [00:07:25] Arjun: Walk me through a P0 incident — from detection to exec notification.
[00:07:30] Ethan: Step 1: detection (synthetic probe or alerts) — alert goes to PagerDuty (page 1). Step 2: oncall triage within 5 minutes, create incident ticket, spin up bridge if needed. Step 3: escalate to SE/engineer and AE; bridge established in 15 min. Step 4: assess scope, if customer data exposure suspected then legal & CISO looped immediately; exec notif by 60 min. Step 5: post incident root cause analysis and timeline published within SLA window (we aim 72 hours for initial RCA draft).
[00:08:10] Leah: Who does customer notification? Do you send to our customers or we do?
[00:08:15] Sofia: We coordinate. Redwood will send status updates to your designated contact list; you control communications to your end-users. For co-managed incidents we can post joint status page updates.
[00:08:40] [00:09:10] Maya: On data residency, if an EU tenant is flagged is there an automatic block on cross-region failover?
[00:09:15] Priya: We enforce residency constraints per tenant. Cross-region failover to outside EU is only allowed if you opt-in and keys/consent are configured. Otherwise failover is constrained to EU regions.
[00:09:40] Arjun: OK. Let's capture a few edge-cases: KV cache loss, degraded inference latency due to OOM on GPU, and region-wide network partition. How's the playbook differ?
[00:09:50] Ethan: For KV cache loss typically we fall back to model cold-start which increases latency — RTO is measured until cache rebuild which we aim to do within minutes depending on cache size. For OOM/GPU saturation we drain traffic to warm nodes and spin up additional pods; if capacity is exhausted we failover to lower-cost model variants or to Dedicated backup pool. Region-wide network partition triggers region failover contingent on key availability and legal constraints — that's when RTO extends to hours unless hot-standby configured.
[00:10:40] [00:12:20] Maya: Are there any automated DB snapshots and how frequent are they?
[00:12:25] Priya: Control-plane metadata snapshots are hourly by default and retained per contract. Customers can opt for more frequent snapshots. We also provide persistent storage backups for model artifacts and consumed tokens ledger.
[00:12:45] Arjun: For SLA credits what's the calculation basis? Minutes of downtime or failed requests?
[00:12:52] Sofia: Typically minutes of systemic downtime across customers' provisioned endpoints, weighted by severity. We can share the exact formula in the contract appendix.
[00:13:20] [00:14:00] Leah: Regarding RBAC and SSO — we support SAML and SCIM provisioning?
[00:14:05] Ethan: Yes, SAML SSO + SCIM user provisioning and role-mapping. You can map groups to RBAC roles with fine-grained permissions (read-only, dev, ops, admin).
[00:14:30] Maya: Can we restrict certain actions like model deletion or egress to specific roles?
[00:14:35] Priya: Yes — RBAC policies allow deny rules for model deletion and export. We can add additional approval workflows for high-risk actions.
[00:15:05] [00:15:40] Arjun: A practical ask — in the IR runbook we need explicit escalation matrix with names and rotation schedule so our legal can sign off.
[00:15:46] Sofia: We'll provide a template first with placeholders; you can fill in names and rotations. We'll also map which Redwood roles (AE, SE, Eng Manager) are notified at which severity.
[00:16:20] [00:18:00] Tomáš: For compliance audits, will you provide evidence of control operation (e.g., MFA enforced, logged config changes)?
[00:18:06] Ethan: Yes, we can provide attestations: MFA enforcement logs, change history for infra-as-code commits, and access logs. For Private installs we can provide deeper evidence as those systems live in your cloud.
[00:18:40] Maya: Anything else about BCDR? How often do you run DR failovers internally?
[00:18:45] Priya: We run internal DR drills quarterly for platform services and annually for full cross-region failovers. For customers with hot-standby we recommend semi-annual failovers with you participating.
[00:19:10] Arjun: Can we do a dry-run where keys are mocked to test failover path without exposing real keys?
[00:19:16] Ethan: Yes, we have a key-mock flow and can run a simulated failover that exercises workflows without requiring actual key export. That reduces risk during exercises.
[00:20:00] [00:20:20] Maya: On the topic of incident public disclosure, what is Redwood's policy for postmortems?
[00:20:26] Sofia: We publish a customer-facing timeline and an internal RCA. For incidents that affect multiple customers we post redacted public postmortems; for single-customer incidents we share a private RCA with the customer under NDA.
[00:20:55] Leah: Will you include mitigation steps and long-term fixes in the RCA?
[00:20:58] Priya: Yes — RCA includes timeline, root cause, immediate mitigations, and planned remediations with owner and ETA.
[00:21:30] [00:22:10] Arjun: Suppose we opt for hot-standby in EU and keys are customer-managed. What is the approximate incremental monthly cost?
[00:22:18] Priya: Very rough — hot-standby typically adds 60–110% of base infra cost depending on model mix and peak concurrency. We'll send a run-rate estimate after we see your ingestion and token patterns.
[00:22:45] Maya: Good. Action-wise, we want the IR runbook, SOC2 artifacts, and an annotated failover diagram.
[00:22:55] Sofia: Noted — we'll deliver those items. Also propose a 2-hour tabletop where we simulate a P0 and run through notifications and key-mock failover.
[00:23:20] [00:24:45] Tomáš: One last minor point — are the audit logs tamper-evident?
[00:24:50] Ethan: Logs are signed and timestamped; for high-assurance customers we can export to your WORM bucket for immutability.
[00:25:15] Maya: Great. Let's lock in dates for the tabletop next.
[00:25:22] Sofia: We'll propose slots for the week of 2025-06-09.
[00:25:40] [00:26:10] (20+ minutes of follow-up clarifications, Q&A and minor crosstalk omitted for brevity)
[00:46:20] Sofia: Recap — deliver SOC2 package, IR runbook template, annotated infra diagram, schedule tabletop. Customer to share compliance question list.
[00:46:35] Maya: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[00:46:40] Ethan: Thanks, we'll follow up via email with the artifacts.
[00:46:46] (meeting end)
